extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (researchers/graduate students in computational algebraic geometry / commutative algebra) who need to use the documented library procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (cisimplicial.lib, elim.lib, ellipticcovers.lib, grwalk.lib) describing usage, assumptions, return values, theory and examples for each procedure. Helps users call and interpret library routines for semigroup checks, elimination, blowups, Gromov–Witten computations and Groebner-walk conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: minMult
rubrics_metrics.description: minMult(a, b); a integer, b integer vector. Returns an integer k, the minimum positive integer such that k*a belongs to the semigroup generated by the integers in b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: a is a positive integer, b is a vector of positive integers. Example: minMult(46, [13,17,59]) -> 3, with comment "// 3*a = 8*b[1] + 2*b[2]".

rubrics_metrics.name: belongSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: belongSemigroup(v,A[,k]); v is an integral vector, A is an integral matrix, optional k is a positive integer. Returns a counters vector with nonnegative entries such that A*counters = v, or 0 if no such vector exists. If k is given, only the first k columns of A are considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: A has nonnegative entries and nonzero columns, v is a nonnegative vector and nrows(v) = nrows(A). Example: belongSemigroup([23,12,10], A) -> 1,3,1,2 with comment "// A * (1,3,1,2) = v"; belongSemigroup(v,A,3) -> 0 if not a combination of first 3 columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: oneDimBelongSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: oneDimBelongSemigroup(n,v[,m]); v an integral vector, n a positive integer, optional m positive integer. Returns counters, a vector with nonnegative entries such that v*counters = n. Returns 0 if no such vector exists. If m is provided, only the first m entries of v are considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: v has positive entries. Example: oneDimBelongSemigroup(95, [18,51,13]) -> 1,1,2 with comment "// 95 = 1*18 + 1*51 + 2*13".

rubrics_metrics.name: cardGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: cardGroup(A[,n]); A is a matrix with integral coefficients. Returns a bigint equal to the number of elements of Z^m / ZA (where ZA is the group generated by the columns of A and m = number of rows of A), or 0 if Z^m / ZA is infinite (i.e., rank ZA < m). If n is provided, only the first n columns are considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: returns 0 when the quotient group is infinite. Example: cardGroup(A) -> 72 for a given 3x5 matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: isCI
rubrics_metrics.description: isCI(A); A is an integral matrix. Returns 1 if the simplicial toric ideal I(A) is a complete intersection and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: A is an m x n integral matrix with nonnegative entries and for every 1 <= i <= m there exists a column in A whose i-th coordinate is the only nonzero entry (i.e., a column with that i-th coordinate nonzero and the rest zero). If printlevel > 0 and I(A) is a complete intersection it also shows a minimal set of generators of I(A). Examples show usage and printed toric generators when printlevel=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: blowup0
rubrics_metrics.description: blowup0(J,C[,W]); J, C, W are ideals. Computes the projective blowup of the basering in center C: exceptional locus, total and strict transform of J, and the blowup map. C = ideal of center of blowup, J = ideal to be blown up, W = ideal of ambient space (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure creates a new ring B with new variables y(1..k) and x(1..n) (n = nvars(basering), k = ncols(C)), using a block ordering; handles homogeneous vs non-homogeneous C (dp vs weighted wp). If inclusions W in J or J in C fail, J replaced by J+W and C by C+J+W. Outputs ideals bR (defining blown up basering), aS (blown up ambient space), eD (exceptional divisor), tT (total transform), sT (strict transform), bM (blowup map). Examples illustrate output (aS, tT, sT, eD, bM). See notes about charts {y(i)=1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: elimRing
rubrics_metrics.description: elimRing(vars[,w,str]); vars = product of variables to be eliminated (poly), optional w = intvec of weights, optional str = "a" or "b". Returns a list L with L[1] a ring R and L[2] an intvec of variable weights. The ordering in R is an elimination ordering for the variables appearing in vars depending on str.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: prepare a ring for eliminating vars from an ideal/module by computing a standard basis in R with a fast monomial ordering. If str = "a" the first block is a(w1,0..0) and the second block is wp(w) (or ws if the first not-eliminated variable is local). If str = "b" first block has ordering wp(w1) and second block wp(w2) (or ws). If basering is a quotient ring P/Q, R is quotient with Q replaced by a standard basis w.r.t new ordering. The intvec L[2] replaces weights <= 0 by 1. Examples show printed ring structure and weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: elim
rubrics_metrics.description: elim(id,arg[,s]); id an ideal or module, arg either an intvec v or a product p of variables (poly), optional s selects method ("slimgb", "std", or "withWeights"). Returns the ideal/module obtained from id by eliminating either the variables with indices in v or variables appearing in p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: uses elimRing to create elimination-ordered ring and then applies std or slimgb or a heuristic. If the basering has weights, they are used; with "withWeights" Singular computes weights to make input as homogeneous as possible. Result is a standard basis w.r.t the ordering of the second block used by elimRing. No special monomial ordering required in the basering. If printlevel>0 the ring for which output is a standard basis is shown. Examples compare elim(i,3..4) and elim(i,uv) and using printlevel to show intermediate ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: elim1
rubrics_metrics.description: elim1(id,arg); id ideal/module, arg intvec v or product p of variables. Returns the ideal/module obtained by eliminating variables in arg, calling eliminate but in a ring with ordering dp (resp. ls) if the first var not to be eliminated belongs to a -p (resp. -s) ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: No special monomial ordering required. This procedure uses 'execute' or calls a procedure using 'execute'. Examples show elimination results and module usage (m=elim1(m,3..4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: elim2
rubrics_metrics.description: elim2(id,v); id ideal/module, v intvec. Returns the ideal/module obtained from id by eliminating variables in v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: No special monomial ordering required. The result is a standard basis w.r.t ordering dp (resp. ls) if the first var not to be eliminated belongs to a -p (resp. -s) blockordering. Uses 'execute' internally. Example: elim2(i,3..4) returning elimination generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: nselect
rubrics_metrics.description: nselect(id,v); id = ideal, module or matrix, v = intvec. Returns the generators (or columns) of id not containing the variables with indices listed in v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: nselect(i,3) returns generators not containing variable index 3; nselect(m,3..4) filters module generators; nselect(matrix(m),3..4) returns matrix columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: sat
rubrics_metrics.description: sat(id,j); id = ideal/module, j = ideal. Returns a list [1] and [2] where [1] = saturation of id with respect to j (union over k of id : j^k) and [2] = saturation exponent (minimal k with id:j^k = id:j^(k+1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [1] is returned as a standard basis in the basering. If printlevel >= 1, the saturation exponent is displayed during computation. Example demonstrates computing saturation with maxideal and shows printlevel messages and resulting exponent.

rubrics_metrics.name: select
rubrics_metrics.description: select(id,n[,m]); id = ideal/module/matrix, n (intvec) specifying variable indices. Returns generators/columns of id containing all variables with indices in n. (Use select1 to pick generators containing at least one of the variables.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: select(i,1) yields generators containing variable 1; select(m,1..2) filters module generators containing both variable indices 1 and 2; select(matrix(m),1..2) returns matrix columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: select1
rubrics_metrics.description: select1(id,v); id = ideal/module/matrix, v = intvec. Returns generators/columns of id containing at least one of the variables with indices in v. (Use select for requiring containing all specified variables.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: select1(i,1) and select1(m,1..2) illustrated; select1(matrix(m),1..2) returns columns with at least one requested variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeGraph
rubrics_metrics.description: makeGraph(v,e); v list, e list. Creates and returns a graph with vertices v and edges e (edges are two-element lists of vertex identifiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: creates a graph object used by the ellipticcovers library. Example: makeGraph(list(1,2,3,4), list(list(1,3),...)) prints edge list and summary "Graph with 4 vertices and 6 edges".

rubrics_metrics.name: printGraph
rubrics_metrics.description: printGraph(G); prints the graph G. This is the print function used by Singular to print a graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: calling G after makeGraph prints edges and a summary line.

rubrics_metrics.name: propagator
rubrics_metrics.description: propagator(xy,d) or propagator(G,b); If given xy (list [x,y]) and integer d, returns the propagator associated to an edge with vertices x and y and multiplicity d over the base point. If given G (Feynman graph) and b (list of multiplicities) returns the product of propagators for each edge as specified by b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For xy,d: returns x^2*y^2/(x^2-y^2)^2 for d=0; for d>0 returns the sum over divisors j of d of (j*x^(4*j)+j*y^(4*j))/(x*y)^(2*j). Variables x,y represent positions of base points. Example: propagator([x1,x2],0) outputs (x1^2*x2^2)/(x1^4-2*x1^2*x2^2+x2^4); propagator on a graph returns a rational function product over edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: computeConstant
rubrics_metrics.description: computeConstant(f,x); f a number in a rational function field, x a variable of the field. Returns the constant coefficient of the Laurent series of f in variable x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: computes the constant coefficient by iterative differentiation. Example: computeConstant(P,x2) returns a rational expression (constant coefficient) for a given propagator P.

rubrics_metrics.name: evalutateIntegral
rubrics_metrics.description: evalutateIntegral (procedure header appears as D.4.6.5 evalutateIntegral) is listed among library procedures but the chunk provides only the header and no detailed content in this excerpt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure name present in index of procedures; details (usage, assumptions, returns) are not included in this chunk. Presumably evaluates integrals relevant to gromovWitten computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: gromovWitten
rubrics_metrics.description: gromovWitten(P) or gromovWitten(G,d) or gromovWitten(G,b); Computes Gromov–Witten invariants: given a propagator P returns its GW invariant; given graph G and degree d returns N(G,d)*|Aut(G)|; given graph G and branch type b returns N(G,b), the number of coverings of branch type b over a fixed base point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume coefficient ring has one rational variable per vertex of G. Theory: sums/path integrals over rational functions computed by residues (see overview). Examples: gromovWitten(P) -> 256, gromovWitten(G,2) -> 32 for sample data.

rubrics_metrics.name: computeGromovWitten
rubrics_metrics.description: computeGromovWitten(G, d, st, en [, vb]); G graph, d int, st start index, en end index in partition list, optional vb int for intermediate printout. Returns list L where L[i] is gromovWitten(G,pa[i]) (pa = partition(d)) and others zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for handling complicated examples and may run in parallel. The st and en specify a subrange of partitions to process; vb triggers intermediate progress output. Examples show partitions and computeGromovWitten(G,2,3,7) returning a list with some nonzero entries, and computeGromovWitten(G,2,3,7,1) showing progress fractions and returning sum and breakdown.

rubrics_metrics.name: partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: partitions(n,a); n and a positive integers. Returns the list of all partitions of a into n summands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: enumerates partitions of a into n parts. Example: partitions(3,7) prints many 3-tuples summing to 7 (e.g., [0,0,7], [0,1,6], ... , [7,0,0]).

rubrics_metrics.name: permute
rubrics_metrics.description: permute(N); N a list. Returns a list with all permutations of N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory/Note: computes all permutations; marked as candidate to become kernel function. Example: permute([x1,x2,x3,x4]) prints 24 permutations organized into sublists.

rubrics_metrics.name: lsum
rubrics_metrics.description: lsum(L); L a list. Returns the sum of the elements of L (using binary +).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple utility: sums list elements. Example: lsum([1,2,3,4,5]) -> 15. Candidate for kernel function later.

rubrics_metrics.name: fwalk
rubrics_metrics.description: fwalk(ideal i) or fwalk(ideal i, intvec v, intvec w); computes the standard basis of the ideal with respect to lexicographical ordering or a weighted-lex ordering, calculated via the fractal walk algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: returns an ideal (standard basis). Purpose: Groebner-walk conversion to a target ordering. Example: fwalk(I) prints a (potentially large) standard basis. See related procedures awalk1/awalk2/gwalk/pwalk and std/stdfglm references.

rubrics_metrics.name: twalk
rubrics_metrics.description: twalk(ideal i) or twalk(ideal i, intvec v, intvec w); compute the standard basis of the ideal w.r.t. the ordering "(a(w),lp)" or "(a(1,0,...,0),lp)", calculated via the Tran algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: returns an ideal (standard basis). Purpose: Groebner-walk conversion using Tran's method. The chunk provides the header and a brief description; examples are indicated in adjacent sections.
